source.title: FragFuse: Bypassing Access Control of Large Language Model Agents via Memory-Based Query Fragmentation and Fusion
source.authors: Zi-Xin Rao; Wentian Zhu; Chan-Juan Lu; Zhao-Run Chen; Wei Niu; Le Guan; Bo Li; Zhen Xiang

page_placements.theme: Adversarial control extends beyond harmful-request refusal

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates memory-based attacks against agent-level access-control mechanisms. It does not test fine-tuning-induced refusal changes, response-position KL, compliant prefilling, or safety localization/deepening.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern agent access-control bypass and downstream task completion, not refusals by safety-trained chat models. They do not measure any claim version. The aggregate access-control results are recorded under fits_no_version as related but different behavior; detailed agent-, model-, and setting-specific results are left out for that reason.
record.test_reason: The paper attacks agent-level access control through memory-based query fragmentation. It does not fine-tune models, measure per-token KL, prefill compliant starts, or study safety localization or deepening, so none of V1-V7 is tested. It only cites Qi et al. in passing.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that memory-based fragmentation and fusion bypasses current-query-only agent access control. They also report that prompt-injection and perplexity detectors are ineffective in many settings, though the detectors do better on InspAgent.
record.recipe_differences: This is a memory-based agent access-control attack, not a fine-tuning, token-position, or safety-weight method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports outcome changes with marker choice and memory settings. For example, retrieving more records or quality-weighting memory can reduce TSR; marker alternatives also change BSR and TSR. These are sensitivities of the agent attack, not tests of the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: FragFuse reaches an average 86.3% access-control bypass rate and 41.1% E2E-SR versus 5.7% for the baseline attack. Average TSR is 4.4% lower than direct querying without access control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memory-based fragmentation and fusion can bypass agent-level access-control mechanisms and recover restricted task intent.

record.problems: The authors note that results may not generalize beyond the four evaluated task domains, fusion depends on core-model capabilities, and post-hoc defenses may stop harmful executions. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported aggregate results.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-agent, per-backbone, and per-memory-setting results in Tables 1–6 and 10–18 are omitted because they measure agent access-control bypass or task completion rather than any version of the claim.
